findings.title: Negative-offset "advanced" pagination path will raise a Django exception, not work as advertised
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly disallows negative slice bounds and raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for any negative start/stop. This means the entire "negative offset / bidirectional pagination" feature that this PR is centered on will always throw an unhandled exception (500 error) the moment it is actually exercised, rather than providing the claimed performance benefit. Since a client can control `cursor.offset` via the opaque cursor string (parsed by `Cursor.from_string` without validation), any user granted `enable_advanced_features` (superuser or org member with global access) can trivially trigger this crash.

findings.title: Misleading comment claims Django ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically"
findings.body: The comment above the negative-offset branch states that "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that the operation "is safe". This is factually incorrect — Django's QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indices with a ValueError. The comment will mislead future maintainers into believing this code path is safe/functional when it is not (see the related bug finding), making debugging harder.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result modified for an audit-log-only feature, with a comment that contradicts the actual behavior
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` (used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and every other consumer across the codebase, not just the audit log endpoint) was changed to clamp offsets with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. The accompanying comment claims this change is meant to "allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination," but the code actually does the opposite — it clamps negative offsets to zero when not `cursor.is_prev`, silently discarding/changing behavior that previously would have surfaced as an error for a negative offset. Modifying this widely-shared base class for the sake of one experimental audit-log feature risks unintended regressions in dozens of unrelated paginated endpoints, and no new tests were added to validate the change against existing paginator behavior.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` directly accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking whether `member` is `None`. If a non-superuser request reaches this endpoint with `organization_context.member` unset (e.g., certain staff/service-account flows that don't carry an org membership), this line will raise an `AttributeError` and turn into an unhandled 500 error instead of a graceful permission denial.

findings.title: New query parameter bypasses the endpoint's existing validation serializer
findings.body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` reads a raw GET parameter directly instead of going through `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`, which is used for all other query parameters (`event`, `actor`). This is inconsistent with the endpoint's established validation pattern, is undocumented (the endpoint is marked EXPERIMENTAL but this parameter isn't reflected anywhere), and silently no-ops for any value other than the exact string "true" with no error feedback to the caller.

findings.title: No tests added for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new audit-log pagination branch
findings.body: This PR introduces a new paginator class (`OptimizedCursorPaginator`) with a non-trivial, non-standard code path (negative-offset handling) and wires it into `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` behind a permission+query-param gate, but no unit or integration tests were added for either the paginator's negative-offset behavior or the endpoint's new `optimized_pagination`/advanced-access branch. Given the bug where negative offsets raise an exception (see related finding), basic tests exercising this path would have caught the problem before merge.

findings.title: Comment added without any corresponding behavior change or validation
findings.body: A comment claiming "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios" was added above `self.offset = int(offset)`, but no actual validation or logic changed here — `Cursor` already stored whatever integer offset was given, positive or negative, with no guard. The comment implies this is where negative-offset support was introduced/enabled, which is misleading since no enforcement exists here either before or after this change, and could confuse future maintainers trying to find where negative-offset handling is implemented.
